title: Practical inspection and evidence assessment
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate independent inspection, proportionate evidence collection and corrective-action closeout
Record factual observations and limitations without compromising privacy or safety
Demonstrate a documented decision, corrective action and verification workflow

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Purpose and scope
instruction.body: Practical inspection and evidence assessment is used to verify agreed cleaning outcomes, not to guarantee sterility, restoration or an outcome beyond the signed scope. Read the work order, site instructions, product constraints and client acceptance criteria. Identify what can be observed safely, what requires specialist authorisation, and which uncertainties must be escalated. Demonstrate independent inspection, proportionate evidence collection and corrective-action closeout.

instruction.heading: Prepare the inspection
instruction.body: Before inspecting, confirm the correct location, work-order version, completion status and any access restrictions. Use a consistent inspection sequence from entrance to exit, top to bottom where appropriate, and clean to dirty. Separate immediate safety hazards from ordinary presentation defects. Choose evidence that is proportionate, lawful and approved by the site. Never disturb hazardous material, open restricted storage or test electrical equipment without authorisation.

instruction.heading: Perform and document
instruction.body: For each finding record the zone and exact location, the agreed criterion, what was observed, when it was observed, and whether it is a defect, a limitation or a question. Distinguish objective observations from interpretation: “visible residue at basin tap base” is preferable to “poor cleaning”. Photograph only when permitted; avoid faces, personal documents and identifying belongings. Never modify an original record to conceal an error.

instruction.heading: Respond and verify
instruction.body: Where the finding is within scope, assign a safe corrective action to an authorised worker, agree priority and record completion. Reinspect the same criterion rather than assuming the problem is resolved. Escalate damage, exposure risks, disputes and work outside the contract. If a product or procedure requires specialist testing, record that testing was not performed; do not invent a result.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace example
instruction.body: A mock client disputes a completed job; present an accurate record without overstating what was verified. A sound response identifies the agreed standard, makes a factual observation, records the limitation, requests approval when required, and communicates the outcome without assigning blame.

instruction.heading: Guided practical
instruction.body: Perform a timed mock inspection and produce a signed evidence portfolio. The learner must explain each choice, identify at least one privacy or safety constraint, record a finding with a timestamp and location, and show how a supervisor would verify any correction.

instruction.heading: Common mistakes and corrections
instruction.body: Avoid treating a photograph as proof of disinfection, confusing a pre-existing defect with a missed task, recording personal information unnecessarily, or closing a finding without reinspection. Correct these by using a scope-linked checklist, objective descriptions, minimum-necessary evidence and a documented closeout step.

instruction.heading: Knowledge and transfer
instruction.body: Explain why the agreed acceptance criterion must be identified before judging a surface. Describe how to record an observation that a different inspector can independently verify. State when inspection must stop and be escalated. Apply the same process to a new site with different privacy and access requirements.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm the correct location, work-order version, completion status and any access restrictions before inspecting.
Read the work order, site instructions, product constraints and client acceptance criteria.
Inspect in a consistent sequence, from entrance to exit and clean to dirty, and separate immediate safety hazards from presentation defects.
For each finding, record the zone, exact location, agreed criterion, what was observed, when, and whether it is a defect, a limitation or a question.
Describe observations objectively, and photograph only where permitted, avoiding faces, personal documents and identifying belongings.
Where a finding is within scope, assign a safe corrective action to an authorised worker and agree its priority.
Reinspect the same criterion before closing a finding, and record that any specialist testing was not performed rather than inventing a result.
Escalate damage, exposure risks, disputes and any work outside the contract, and stop inspecting when escalation is required.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: The work order version, completion status and access restrictions are confirmed before inspecting.
Photos and records stay limited to what is needed, are collected legally and are cleared by the site, and must not capture people's faces, papers or possessions.
Each finding is recorded with a timestamp, location, criterion and category.
Corrective actions are reinspected against the same criterion before they are closed.
summary: A practical inspection starts from the work order, site instructions and client acceptance criteria, and identifies what can be observed safely.
Evidence is collected in proportion and kept approved and lawful, with personal information excluded and original records never altered to hide an error.
The inspection closes with a timed, documented record in which corrections are reinspected and no verification is overstated.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a practical inspection finding be checked against before it is called a defect?
options: Whether the photo looks clean enough to be filed and whether the room was tidy when the crew arrived
Whether the worker who cleaned it is available to be asked and whether they agree with the finding
Whether the client has already paid and whether the client has complained before about the work
The agreed acceptance criterion and the exact location, checked against the correct work-order version

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the inspector record when a finding cannot be photographed without exposing private information?
options: Keep the photo on your personal phone so it can be checked later and share it with the team
Upload it to a public site so the client can see the finding and share the link with the team
Record the finding in objective words and use only the minimum necessary, permitted evidence
Send it to the client's manager, who can decide whether to keep it and the full image is kept on file

knowledgeChecks.question: What is needed before a corrective action from a practical inspection is closed?
options: Once it has been reinspected against the same criterion and the completion recorded
Once the worker says it has been fixed and the client has been told it is done
Once a photograph has been taken and the photo has been sent to the client
Once the client stops asking about it and the crew has left the site today
